name: Salmon & cheese patties (salmon-swap of the tuna version)

source.author: Hebrew recipe (screenshot), adapted
source.notes: Salmon swap of tuna_cheese_patties — canned salmon replaces the 2 cans of tuna; everything else identical. Removes the mercury flag and adds omega-3 + vitamin D. Best with bone-in canned salmon (soft edible bones add calcium + vitamin D). Values assume ~280 g drained canned salmon. Method not shown (baked assumed).

steps: Mix drained (flaked) salmon, cottage cheese, Shkedi cheese, beaten eggs, breadcrumbs, chopped onion, grated yellow cheese, salt and pepper.
Form patties and bake (or pan-fry) until set and golden. (Method not shown — baked assumed.)

him.verdict: The better version for your sperm goal. You give up a little protein vs the tuna (26 vs 29 g/serving, still ~9 g protein per 100 kcal) and gain ~14 g of mostly-healthy fat — but that fat brings ~650 mg omega-3 EPA/DHA AND ~230 IU vitamin D per serving, TWO of your sperm-priority micros the tuna version barely had. Plus more calcium. Same cheese-driven sodium; yellow cheese is still the lever.
suggested_mods: Use bone-in canned salmon — the soft bones add calcium + vitamin D at no effort
Bake, not fry; drop/halve the yellow cheese to trim sodium/fat
Serve over greens for fiber + folate

her_preconception.verdict: This swap turns the tuna patties from a flagged 'sometimes' dish into a clean preconception winner. NO mercury flag — canned salmon is a low-mercury fish — and it adds DHA (~650 mg omega-3, key for fetal brain development), vitamin D, and calcium on top of the protein + choline + selenium. Fully cooked, pasteurized cheeses, no safety flags left. This is the version to make for her.
prenatal_highlights: vitamin D (~230 IU) + calcium (~270 mg, more with bone-in salmon)
low-mercury fish — mercury flag removed vs the tuna version
suggested_mods: Prefer bone-in canned salmon for the calcium/vitamin-D bump
This is the strictly-better preconception version — make this instead of the tuna one

cooking_guide: Drain the canned salmon well; if it's bone-in, mash the soft bones right into the mix (extra calcium — you won't feel them).
Flake the salmon and mix with the cheeses, eggs, breadcrumbs and grated onion; season with salt, pepper, a squeeze of lemon and fresh dill (dill loves salmon).
If the mix is wet, add breadcrumbs until it holds; chill 15-20 min.
Form patties and bake at 200 C (400 F) ~20 min, flipping once, until golden — or pan-fry for a crisper crust.
Rest a few minutes before serving.
Tip: a little lemon zest in the mix makes the salmon taste fresh instead of 'canned'.
